strengths: Addresses a timely, important problem in a rapidly growing field with strong motivation for taxonomy unification
Comprehensive systematic methodology covering 134 papers across 9 databases with clear inclusion criteria and multi-dimensional analysis
Well-structured taxonomy with useful novel distinctions (in-generation, in-context attribution) that effectively organizes fragmented literature
Extensive evaluation analysis of 300 metrics categorized across 7 dimensions and 6 methods, identifying fragmentation in common frameworks/benchmarks
Practical resource compilation (231 datasets, 17 frameworks, 11 benchmarks) with promised public release provides genuine community value
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (taxonomy diagram, evaluation metrics overview) that communicate complex information well
Systematic methodology following established guidelines (Petersen et al. 2008) demonstrates rigor in conducting the survey
weaknesses: Limited critical evaluation beyond description: no assessment of which approaches perform best, lack of tradeoff analysis (cost vs. accuracy, coverage vs. precision), and minimal discussion of failure modes or approach limitations

Shallow analysis of key findings: field dominance patterns (126 non-parametric vs. 25 parametric papers) unexplored, extreme framework fragmentation (only 2 reused) not critically examined, concentrated dataset usage not discussed as limitation

Questionable categorization scheme: distinction between Model-Centric (3 papers) and Data-Centric (4 papers) poorly justified, with both involving learning modifications; sparse category populations question meaningfulness of distinctions

Novelty primarily organizational: taxonomy heavily builds on prior work (Huang and Chang 2024), identified gaps are somewhat obvious, and solutions in Section 7 remain largely prescriptive statements rather than actionable insights

Evaluation analysis limitations: 300 metrics cataloged but missing validity/reliability analysis, no guidance on metric appropriateness for different tasks, Figure 7 dense and difficult to parse, complementary metrics concept underdeveloped

Search strategy and scope constraints: limited to three keywords (citation, attribution, quote) potentially missing related work using different terminology; February 2025 cutoff with only 10 papers limits trend claims; no analysis of literature biases across languages/domains/geographies

Absent empirical comparisons: no systematic comparison of methods on common benchmarks, no cost-performance analysis, missing guidance for practitioners on methodology selection, no discussion of approach performance across LLM scales

Methodological transparency gaps: inter-annotator agreement not quantified, annotation scheme details sparse, limited discussion of annotation bias or disagreement resolution; reproducibility concerns despite promised public release

strengths: Rigorous methodology following PRISMA 2020 with excellent inter-annotator agreement (α=1.0 on screening, 0.77-1.0 on taxonomy)
Comprehensive and timely coverage of 134 papers across a rapidly growing field, with systematic analysis of 300 metrics, 231 datasets, 19 frameworks, and 11 benchmarks
Well-designed multidimensional faceted taxonomy that captures field complexity without artificial constraints across three orthogonal dimensions
Practical contributions including evaluation guidelines (Table 1) that usefully distinguish core vs. contextual dimensions and provide informed metric selection guidance
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (taxonomy, metric overview) and extensive appendices providing valuable detailed analysis
Publicly available annotated dataset and comprehensive resource compilation that will serve as reference for the field
Identifies concrete standardization gaps (only 2 frameworks reused despite 19 existing) with actionable insights for future work
weaknesses: Limited analytical depth: paper is primarily descriptive and cataloging; lacks causal analysis of why approaches are chosen, which work best, or systematic analysis of trade-offs

No experimental validation: lacks comparative effectiveness analysis, statistical significance testing of trends, or empirical comparison of approaches; claims about evaluation utility are not validated
Significant task representation bias: QA dominates with 71% of papers (95/134); findings may be heavily QA-biased with limited discussion of generalizability to underrepresented tasks

Shallow evaluation framework analysis: documents fragmentation (only 2/19 frameworks reused) but provides limited analysis of why, no recommendations for framework adoption, and missing design principles

Missing critical comparative analysis: no systematic comparison of citation style effectiveness, no cost-benefit analysis, no computational efficiency discussion, no error analysis of existing approaches
Limited quantitative analysis: no correlation analysis between evaluation dimensions, no metric clustering, no statistical testing of temporal trends, no analysis of dimension interactions
Reproducibility gaps: inter-annotator agreement computed only on 30/134 papers, disagreement resolution underspecified, some taxonomy ambiguities (e.g., passage vs. other citation styles)
